_comment: Semantic token → palette step map for DARK mode, retuned to the approved MyCSC dark theme v2 spec (neutral dark-gray surfaces, no near-blacks; elevation reads from progressively lighter surfaces + hairline borders, not shadows). The surface ladder + neutral borders/text draw from the hand-tuned dark-neutral `slate` ramp (values are the spec's neutrals verbatim; `slate-850` was added for the inset/muted tier). Interactive roles draw from THEIR OWN family's lightened steps (primary fills/ring on primary-300/200, links on link-200/100), same shape as the status families — NOT from the spec's vivid accent teal (ADR-0034): borrowing accent-500/400/300 matched the MyCSC dark v2 spec's #3BB8B0/#56CFC8/#8AE0DA but broke ADR-0011's per-family re-theming (re-seeding `primary` could not move dark fills). Deep navy-teal fills (nav chrome, subtle fills) stay on primary steps, one step lighter than light mode. Verified with scripts/audit-contrast.mjs. Keep keys in sync with light.json. Mode-invariant roles (inverse-*) live in invariant.json.
_comment-inverted: Inverted-surface tier (ADR-0032): white pill on the dark page. Each status *-inverted role is the family's accent ink on white (coloured icon + alpha-wash halo — the wash lands on the pale subtle tint the light-mode alerts use); neutral inks reuse light mode's on-surface neutrals. Keep keys in sync with light.json.
_comment-chart: Chart tokens (ADR-0030): frozen viz-owned literals, re-validated against the dark chart surface (slate-800) — dark steps are selected, not flipped. Same hue per slot as light mode (series identity is mode-stable). Slots 1/2/5/9/10 equal today's info-500/secondary-400/accent-600/info-400/secondary-300. Slots 2/3/4/6 sit in the sub-3:1 contrast relief band on slate-800: legal only with a relief channel (direct labels, tooltips, or a table view) — documented in the dataviz guide.
_comment-logo: Dark logo per the MyCSC dark spec: near-white star + wordmark with the magenta kite kept as a brightened literal (fixed brand mark, like the light-mode literals — off the palette so consumer re-seeding cannot recolor it).
